prompt.context_jp: 東京オリンピックの開催決定に沸く東京で、不動産業界___かつてない活況を呈していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東京オリンピックの開催決定に沸く東京で、不動産業界___かつてない活況を呈していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence introduces the real estate industry as the topic being described — it's a general statement about its state. は frames it as 'as for the real estate industry'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the industry as new information in a specific event ('it was the real estate industry that...'), which doesn't match this descriptive narration.

contrast_examples.jp: 不動産業界は活況だった。
contrast_examples.en: The real estate industry was booming. (topical description)

contrast_examples.jp: 不動産業界が活況だった。
contrast_examples.en: It was the real estate industry that was booming. (identifying which industry)

prompt.context_jp: 夜___明け、新宿の街にまた慌ただしい一日が始まろうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夜___明け、新宿の街にまた慌ただしい一日が始まろうとしていた。

feedback.correct_en: 'Dawn breaking' is a neutral event being reported — a new scene opening. が marks this fresh event description.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'night' a contrastive topic ('as for night, it broke...'), which sounds unnatural for scene-setting.

contrast_examples.en: It started raining. (event report)
As for rain, it didn't fall. (topical/contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 白洲美加___、仕事の準備をせずに、スマートフォンの画面ばかり眺めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 白洲美加___、仕事の準備をせずに、スマートフォンの画面ばかり眺めていた。

feedback.correct_en: Mika has already been introduced as a known character; this sentence describes what she (as topic) was doing. は fits topical description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single her out as new or exhaustive ('it was Mika who...'), which doesn't match the storytelling flow here.

contrast_examples.jp: 美加はスマホを見ていた。
contrast_examples.en: Mika was looking at her phone. (describing her)

contrast_examples.jp: 美加がスマホを見ていた。
contrast_examples.en: It was Mika who was looking at the phone. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外では、真夏の日差し___すでにアスファルトを焼き始めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外では、真夏の日差し___すでにアスファルトを焼き始めていた。

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-painting description — a new element (the sunlight) is introduced into the picture. が marks neutral description of what's happening.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the sunlight into a known topic being contrasted, but it's being newly described in the scene.

contrast_examples.en: The wind was blowing. (scenic description)

contrast_examples.jp: 風は吹いていなかった。
contrast_examples.en: As for wind, it wasn't blowing. (topical/contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 最後の問いかけの後、室内___は気まずい沈黙が流れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最後の問いかけの後、室内___は気まずい沈黙が流れた。

feedback.correct_en: 流れる with an abstract subject like 沈黙 takes に to mark the location where the state exists/arises. 室内には気まずい沈黙が流れた is the fixed collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the site of an active action, but 'silence flowing' describes a state settling into a place — に is the natural choice.

contrast_examples.en: Silence fell in the room.
We held a meeting in the room. (active action → で)

prompt.context_jp: 不動産屋の正念場___土日です。
prompt.prompt_jp: 不動産屋の正念場___土日です。

feedback.correct_en: This is a definitional topic-comment: 'As for a realtor's crunch time, it's the weekend.' は sets 正念場 as the topic being defined.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reverse the focus ('the crunch time is what the weekend is'), which doesn't match Sangenya's declarative statement.

contrast_examples.en: My hobby is reading. (A は B definition)
I am Tanaka. (identifying answer to 'who is Tanaka?')

prompt.context_jp: 宅間と美加の腕___は、三千枚ものチラシの束がずっしりとのしかかっている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宅間と美加の腕___は、三千枚ものチラシの束がずっしりとのしかかっている。

feedback.correct_en: のしかかる 'to weigh down upon' takes に to mark where the weight is landing. 腕に…のしかかっている = 'weighs down upon their arms'.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the site of an action, but this is about where the burden rests — に is required with のしかかる.

contrast_examples.jp: 肩に荷物がのしかかる。
contrast_examples.en: The burden weighs on my shoulders.
To carry the load with/on one's shoulder (active action).

prompt.context_jp: 彼はいつでも誰にでも優しい___、その優しさの内側は誰にも読めない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼___いつでも誰にでも優しいが、その優しさの内側___誰にも読めない。
prompt.prompt_en: Both blanks take the same particle. Choose it.

feedback.correct_en: Both clauses contrast two sides of Adachi: he (topic) is kind, but his kindness (contrastive topic) can't be read. は fits both the topic and the contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce them as new information or exhaustive answers, but the sentence is clearly a topical contrast between surface and inner self.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔はいいが、性格は悪い。
contrast_examples.en: His face is good, but his personality is bad. (contrastive は)
I like people whose faces are nice. (relative-clause が)

prompt.context_jp: 「お父さんしか 離婚する人___いないでしょ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お父さんしか 離婚する人___いないでしょ」

feedback.correct_en: Wait — reconsider. しか…ない structures require は or nothing before 離婚する人. Actually 離婚する人 is modified; the main predicate いない needs the subject marked. With しか the standard particle is omitted/は. 'お父さんしか...人はいない' — は is the natural reading highlighting absence besides Dad.
feedback.incorrect_en: が in this しか…ない exclusive negation sounds off; the pattern is XしかYはない / Xしかいない.

contrast_examples.en: Only he knows.
That's the only way.

prompt.context_jp: 「土地も家も私の名義です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いいえ 土地___家___私の名義です」
prompt.prompt_en: Both blanks share the same particle. Choose it.

feedback.correct_en: Kimiko emphasizes 'BOTH land AND house' are in her name — the additive も fits perfectly ('X も Y も').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would list two separate contrastive topics; here she's bundling them together as both belonging to her.

contrast_examples.en: Both my father and mother are well.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は元気だが、母は病気だ。
contrast_examples.en: Father is well, but mother is sick. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「万事 私___お任せください」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「万事 私___お任せください」

feedback.correct_en: 任せる 'to entrust to' takes に to mark the recipient. 私にお任せください = 'please leave it to me'.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would mark a direct object (what is entrusted), but 万事 already serves that role here — the person entrusted takes に.

contrast_examples.en: Entrust the work to him.
Leave the rest to me.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の決め台詞。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___売れない家はありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes Sangenya's signature line.

feedback.correct_en: Her trademark line is 「私に売れない家はありません」— 'there is no house I cannot sell'. The に marks the agent in a potential-form negation.
feedback.incorrect_en: で/を don't form the correct potential-agent frame; this fixed catchphrase uses に.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼に解けない問題はない。
contrast_examples.en: There is no problem he can't solve.

contrast_examples.jp: 私にできることはやる。
contrast_examples.en: I'll do what I can do.

prompt.context_jp: 居間には、壁掛け時計の針の音___響いている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 居間には、壁掛け時計の針の音だけ___響いている。

feedback.correct_en: だけが emphasizes exhaustively 'only the clock sound (and nothing else) echoes' — が marks the sole subject in neutral description.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would imply contrast with other situations, but here the point is simply that only one sound existed in the room.

contrast_examples.en: Only he knows. (exhaustive)
Today alone is special. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: そのとき、玄関の引き戸___開く音がした。
prompt.prompt_jp: そのとき、玄関の引き戸___開く音がした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the relative clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 音, the subject of 開く takes が. は generally cannot appear as the subject of a relative clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は is for main-clause topics, not for subjects embedded inside a noun-modifying clause.

contrast_examples.en: A picture a child drew. (relative-clause が)
The child drew a picture. (main-clause は)

prompt.context_jp: 美加が実家について訴える場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この家は私が育った ___の家なんです！」

feedback.correct_en: 思い出の家 'house of memories' is the natural collocation for a childhood home full of personal history.
feedback.incorrect_en: 記念 ('commemoration') and 記録 ('records') don't collocate with 家 in this emotional, nostalgic sense.

contrast_examples.en: A place full of memories.
A commemorative photo.

prompt.context_jp: 父が離婚について諦めるように言うことわざ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___盆に返らず」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes this proverb.

feedback.correct_en: 覆水盆に返らず 'spilled water doesn't return to the tray' = 'what's done is done'. A set proverb.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流水/冷水 are real words but don't form this fixed proverb.

contrast_examples.en: No use crying over spilled milk.
Regret comes too late.

prompt.context_jp: 「物件の所有者___白洲貴美子様です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「物件の所有者___白洲貴美子様です」

feedback.correct_en: Sangenya is making an A は B definitional statement about who the owner is as the topic. 'As for the owner, it is Ms. Shirasu.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is Kimiko?' by identifying her as the owner — the reverse focus. Here 所有者 is the known topic.

contrast_examples.en: The president is Mr. Tanaka. (defining the president)
Mr. Tanaka is the president. (identifying who)

prompt.context_jp: 「私の仕事___家を売ることです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私の仕事___家を売ることです」

feedback.correct_en: Classic A は B self-definition: 'My job is to sell houses.' は presents 私の仕事 as the topic being defined.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would say 'it is my job that is to sell houses' — a strange exhaustive reading not fitting her matter-of-fact declaration.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の夢は医者になることだ。
contrast_examples.en: My dream is to become a doctor.
That is my dream. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 「家族っていうの___ 記憶だと思うんだよね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「家族っていうの___ 記憶だと思うんだよね」

feedback.correct_en: Yashiro defines 'family' as a general concept: 'family IS memories'. ~というのは is the fixed topic-defining frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't form the standard definitional phrase; ~というのが works only in rare specifying contexts, not in a general philosophical statement.

contrast_examples.jp: 愛というのは難しいものだ。
contrast_examples.en: Love is a difficult thing. (definitional)
That is love. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 社員たちが怒られたあとの描写。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朝の叱責から___ように、社員たちは次々と営業所を後にした。

feedback.correct_en: 叱責から逃げる 'to flee from a scolding' is the natural collocation — the employees physically leave to escape the morning's rebuke.
feedback.incorrect_en: 隠れる 'to hide' needs a place, and 避ける doesn't fit with から in the same escape-oriented sense.

contrast_examples.en: To flee from reality.
To avoid danger.

prompt.context_jp: 自分が指されなかったときの安堵。
prompt.prompt_jp: ほかの社員たちは、自分に矛先が向かなかったことに、そっと胸を___下ろしていた。

feedback.correct_en: 胸をなで下ろす 'to stroke one's chest downward' is a set idiom meaning 'to breathe a sigh of relief'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 押さえる or 叩く with 胸 produce different (or non-idiomatic) meanings — only なで下ろす forms the relief idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: ほっと胸をなで下ろす。
contrast_examples.en: To breathe a sigh of relief.
To be proud (lit. puff out one's chest).

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の丁寧なビジネス表現。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「売却依頼書に ご___いただけますか？」

feedback.correct_en: ご署名いただけますか is the standard polite business request for a signature on a document.
feedback.incorrect_en: ご記入 is used for filling in forms generally, and ご書き is not a natural polite form. For a 'signature' specifically, 署名 is correct.

contrast_examples.jp: こちらにご署名ください。
contrast_examples.en: Please sign here.

contrast_examples.jp: 必要事項をご記入ください。
contrast_examples.en: Please fill in the required items.

prompt.context_jp: 庭野の自嘲的な告白。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「自分は その人に 相手に___ていないので」

feedback.correct_en: 相手にされない 'to be given no attention / be ignored' is a fixed passive idiom. Niwano means Sangenya doesn't even register him.
feedback.incorrect_en: 相手になる means 'to become a match for'; 相手にできる isn't a standard pattern here.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰にも相手にされない。
contrast_examples.en: Nobody takes me seriously.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の相手になる人はいない。
contrast_examples.en: Nobody can match him.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が庭野に放った冷たい一言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「少しくらい 私のことを知ったからといって⇒ ___になるな！」

feedback.correct_en: いい気になる 'to get carried away / full of oneself' is a set phrase. Sangenya tells him not to presume on a bit of information.
feedback.incorrect_en: いい顔/いい子 do form phrases but don't carry the 'getting cocky' nuance that fits her rebuke.

contrast_examples.jp: 褒められていい気になる。
contrast_examples.en: To get full of oneself from praise.
To not look pleased.

prompt.context_jp: エレベーターで美加が足立をデートに誘う。
prompt.prompt_jp: Which sounds most natural for Mika's invitation to Adachi (coworker, slightly flirtatious)?

choices.text: 「今夜 お仕事終わったあと ごはん一緒に行きません？」
「今夜 お仕事終了後 ごはんを食べに参りませんか？」
「今夜 仕事終わってから めし行こうぜ」

feedback.correct_en: The story line (a) matches the register: polite but warm, suited to a slightly flirty invitation to a male coworker.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too stiff/formal (business language) and (c) is too blunt/masculine for a woman inviting her crush.

contrast_examples.en: Shall we go together? (friendly polite)
Would you come along? (very stiff keigo)

prompt.context_jp: 貴美子が離婚の経緯を話す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: Which version sounds most natural for 'he suddenly brought it up'?

choices.text: お父さんが 突然言い出したの
お父さんが 突然話し始めたの
お父さんが 急に発言したの

feedback.correct_en: 言い出す 'to blurt out / bring up' naturally fits the sudden announcement of a divorce — matches the story's line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 話し始める is too neutral ('started talking'); 発言する is formal/public and off-register for a private family conversation.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に別れたいと言い出した。
contrast_examples.en: He suddenly said he wanted to break up.
To speak up at a meeting. (formal)

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が初対面の客に自己紹介する。
prompt.prompt_jp: Which self-introduction sounds most natural in business?

choices.text: 三軒家万智と申します
三軒家万智と言います

feedback.correct_en: 〜と申します is the standard humble self-introduction in business, matching Sangenya's professional stance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜と言います is polite but less formal than business standards, and だよ is casual and inappropriate for first-time client meetings.

contrast_examples.en: I am Yamada. (business humble)
I'm Yamada. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: 父親が娘に、取り返しがつかないことを伝える。
prompt.prompt_jp: Which phrasing is most natural to express 'what's done is done'?

choices.text: もう元には戻せないという意味だ
水をこぼしたらお盆に戻らないよ

feedback.correct_en: The father quotes the fixed four-character proverb 覆水盆に返らず — compact and literary, fitting his resigned tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is a plain paraphrase missing the proverb's weight; (c) is a literal, unnatural reading of the proverb's imagery.

contrast_examples.en: Spilled water doesn't return to the tray.

contrast_examples.jp: もう取り返しがつかない。
contrast_examples.en: It can no longer be undone. (plain paraphrase)

prompt.context_jp: 美加が三軒家にお願いする場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: Which version sounds most natural as a sincere plea?

choices.text: 私に 私の実家を売らせてください！
私が私の実家を売ることを許可してほしい！
私の実家を売る権利をください！

feedback.correct_en: The causative-request 〜させてください 'please let me do X' is the natural, emotional way to ask permission to take on the task.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) and (c) are stiff, bureaucratic alternatives that lose the direct, pleading tone of the scene.

contrast_examples.en: Please let me do it.
Please give me permission to do it. (bureaucratic)
